summary: You had an emergency room visit on May 30, 2026, at St. Adelaide Regional Medical Center (out-of-network). Because of the No Surprises Act, you are protected and pay the same cost-sharing (copay and coinsurance) as if the provider were in-network. Your plan paid $584. You owe $396 in total: a $250 emergency room copay and $146 in coinsurance (your percentage share of the allowed amount).

lines.explanation: You owe a $250 copay for this emergency room visit. [CODE-PR-3: "PR-3 means this amount is a copay, a fixed dollar amount for a covered visit or service."] [PLAN-COPAY: "The emergency room copay is $250, waived if you are admitted to the hospital."] You were not admitted, so the copay applies.

citations.quote: PR-3 means this amount is a copay, a fixed dollar amount for a covered visit or service.
The emergency room copay is $250, waived if you are admitted to the hospital.

lines.explanation: You owe $146 in coinsurance. [CODE-PR-2: "PR-2 means this amount is coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount after the deductible is met."] After your copay, you pay this percentage of the allowed amount ($980). The plan paid the rest.

citations.quote: PR-2 means this amount is coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount after the deductible is met.

lines.explanation: The provider billed $2,400, but the allowed amount (the maximum the plan recognizes) is $980. The difference of $1,420 is marked CO-45. [CODE-CO-45: "CO-45 means the provider billed more than the rate they agreed to with the plan. The difference is written off by the provider. Members do not owe CO-45 amounts for in-network care."] Because this is an out-of-network emergency, the No Surprises Act applies—you should not owe the $1,420 overage. Verify with the provider that they are not billing you for this difference.

citations.quote: CO-45 means the provider billed more than the rate they agreed to with the plan. The difference is written off by the provider. Members do not owe CO-45 amounts for in-network care.

actions: Review this EOB to confirm the plan paid $584 and your cost-sharing ($250 copay + $146 coinsurance = $396 total) matches.
Before paying any provider bill, verify that the provider is not asking you to pay the $1,420 overage (marked CO-45). Under the No Surprises Act, this amount should be written off.
Keep this EOB with your records in case the provider attempts to bill you for amounts outside your cost-sharing.
